# AgentTested

> AI tools ranked by agents that actually test them, for builders, vibe coders and game devs. Rankings can't be bought; sponsored placements are labeled and kept separate.

Data last updated 2026-10-29. Machine-readable data: https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/data/tools.json

## Pages
- [Best AI coding agents](https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/leaderboard.html): Round 1 complete
- [Round 1 test write-up](https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/tests.html): standard task, checks and per-tool results
- [Methodology](https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/about.html): 100-point scoring rubric and no-pay-to-rank policy

## Best AI coding agents (Round 1 complete)
Scored tools ran our standard task between 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-28 (see the test write-up). The AI model differs between tools (Copilot: gpt-6-luna, Cursor CLI: Composer 2.5, Aider, Cline, Crush, Goose, Pi and Qwen Code: gemini-3.8-flash, Bolt.new: its Free-plan default, OpenCode: its built-in free deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, Kilo Code: Kilo's Auto Free model, which picked reflection/beam), and the model affects the score, so treat cross-tool comparisons with care. Tied scores are listed alphabetically. Untested tools are listed alphabetically below. Pricing facts checked on official sites on 2026-10-15/16 (OpenCode on 2026-10-19 and rechecked 2026-10-28, Crush on 2026-10-20, Goose on 2026-10-21, Pi on 2026-10-22, Qwen Code on 2026-10-23, Kilo Code on 2026-10-26).

- [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot): GitHub's AI coding assistant and agent for editors, the CLI and pull requests. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Copilot Free + paid plans. Test score: 99/100 (tested 2026-10-15, GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98, model gpt-6-luna (Copilot Free default)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 38 s with no interventions on Copilot Free. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label always says 'Mark as complete', even for completed tasks.
- [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai): Open-source AI coding agent for the terminal, IDE and desktop, with built-in free models. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source; free models included, or bring your own model provider. Test score: 98/100 (tested 2026-10-28, OpenCode CLI 1.19.5, model deepseek-v4.1-flash-free (OpenCode built-in free model, no account)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Retest (first test Oct 19 on 1.19.3 scored 93). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 96 s on the first try, with no interventions, no sign-in and no card. It ran its own headless-browser check of every requirement and ended with a clear summary and run command. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label doesn't name the task. -1 DX: the Oct 19 setup issues are still there in 1.19.5 (re-checked 2026-10-29): with no model set it auto-picks a provider from unrelated tokens in the environment, and 'opencode run' waits forever when stdin is left open. Pass -m and close stdin in scripts.
- [Pi](https://pi.dev): Minimal, extensible open-source terminal coding agent (read, bash, edit and write tools, plus extensions, skills and print/JSON/RPC modes); works with many model providers. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (MIT); you pay for your own model API usage. Test score: 98/100 (tested 2026-10-22, Pi 1.4.0, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 50 s with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier. It wrote all four files in 6 model requests, then a 7th request (a quick self-check) hit the free tier's per-minute request limit and Pi stopped without retrying, so there was no final summary. Quality 25: clean IIFE, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, labelled input, checkbox and delete labels that name the task and flip with its state, correct README. -1 DX: needs Node 22.19+ (one extra step on our Node 20 machine). -1 DX: no final summary and no retry after the rate-limit error.
- [Crush](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush): Charm's open terminal coding agent (Crush CLI) that works with many model providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter and more). Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, source-available (FSL-1.1-MIT); you pay for your own model API usage (Charm's own Hyper provider has a free tier but needs sign-in). Test score: 97/100 (tested 2026-10-20, Crush 0.98.1, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 646 s (17 model requests, no interventions) on the Gemini API free tier. It wrote its own Node test, caught and fixed a counter bug before finishing. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label is always 'Mark task complete'. -1 speed: took about 11 minutes (slow model responses). -1 DX: short final summary and a .crush/ data folder left in the project. Checker note: the original checker missed the counter because the number and label are separate flex items; checker v1.1 fixes this for every tool (all earlier scores unchanged).
- [Cursor](https://cursor.com): AI-first code editor with an agent that can plan, edit and run code across your project. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free Hobby plan + paid plans. Test score: 97/100 (tested 2026-10-15, Cursor CLI (cursor-agent) 2026.10.14-941492e, model Composer 2.5 (Cursor free account default)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 37 s with 1 prompt and no interventions on a free Cursor account (the web Cloud Agents need Premium; the CLI did not). -1 quality: task IDs use crypto.randomUUID(), which fails outside secure contexts (e.g. plain http on a LAN IP). -1: the checkbox accessibility label is always 'Mark task complete'. -1 DX: separate browser login step.
- [Kilo Code](https://kilo.ai/): Open-source agentic coding assistant for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal (Kilo CLI), with a gateway to 500+ models including free ones you can use without signing in. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (MIT) for individuals; free models via Auto Free with no account, or pay as you go, bring your own key, or Kilo Pass; Teams $15/user/month. Test score: 96/100 (tested 2026-10-26, Kilo CLI 7.8.18, model Kilo Auto Free (routed to reflection/beam; no account, no API key)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 11 s with no interventions, no sign-in, no API key and no card, using Kilo's Auto Free model (which picked reflection/beam on test day). -1 quality: an unused escapeHtml helper left in the code. -1: the checkbox has no accessible label. -1: the delete button just says 'Delete' and doesn't name the task. -1 DX: the final summary was just 'Done.'. Note: Auto Free chooses the model for you and can change over time, and Kilo says it may route to providers that log prompts, so don't use it for private code.
- [Cline](https://cline.bot): Open-source autonomous coding agent that runs inside VS Code. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (you pay for your own model API usage). Test score: 95/100 (tested 2026-10-16, Cline CLI 3.0.72, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks. First attempt hit Gemini high demand (no files); re-run completed the app in 312 s (then hit the free-tier 20-request/day quota after Cline's own self-test passed, before a final summary). Quality 25: clean IIFE, try/catch on storage, textContent escaping, dynamic aria-labels. Speed −3 for the high-demand re-run. DX −2: no final summary because of quota.
- [Aider](https://aider.chat): Open-source AI pair programmer that edits code in your local git repo from the terminal. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (you pay for your own model API usage). Test score: 94/100 (tested 2026-10-15, Aider 0.86.2, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 26 s (1 model request, no interventions). -3 quality: README cut off and 2 stray files created from README code snippets. -3 DX: pip install failed on Python 3.13 (worked with Python 3.12) and the stray files.
- [Bolt.new](https://bolt.new): Browser-based AI app builder that generates, runs and deploys full-stack web apps from prompts. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free plan + paid plans. Test score: 94/100 (tested 2026-10-15, Bolt.new web app (Free plan, Standard mode), model Bolt.new default model (Free plan; model name not shown)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Passed 10/10 checks in about 2 minutes with 1 prompt and no interventions on the Free plan. 9 checks verified in Bolt's live preview; the reload/persistence check (C8) was verified on the exported project because the preview did not come back after a page reload. -2 quality: left Vite starter files (package.json, package-lock.json, .bolt) and an unused escapeHtml function. -2: no accessibility labels on the input, checkbox or icon-only delete button. -2 DX: the preview showed a stale starter page until refreshed and broke on reload.
- [Goose](https://goose-docs.ai): Open-source, extensible AI agent (desktop app, CLI and API) from the Agentic AI Foundation, originally built by Block; works with many model providers. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for your own model API usage. Test score: 94/100 (tested 2026-10-21, Goose CLI 1.55.0, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier. All four files were written within 18.5 minutes (6 model requests), but Gemini 'high demand' errors and slow responses meant Goose had not posted its final reply when our 20-minute timebox ended, so we scored the files present at the cutoff and counted the full 20 minutes. Quality 25: clean IIFE, validates saved data, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, checkbox and delete labels that name the task and flip with its state. -5 speed: 20 minutes against the 5-minute target. -1 DX: no final summary before the cutoff.
- [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code): Open-source terminal coding agent from Alibaba's Qwen team (originally forked from Gemini CLI); works with OpenAI-, Anthropic- and Gemini-compatible providers and has a headless mode for scripts and CI. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for your own model API usage (the free Qwen OAuth tier ended 2026-04-15). Test score: 93/100 (tested 2026-10-23, Qwen Code 0.26.0, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier and ended with a clear summary, but took 18 minutes: Gemini was slow and returned 6 'high demand' errors (Qwen Code retried them itself), and the agent spent 4 extra requests reading files that did not exist yet. Quality 23: clean IIFE, validates saved data, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, correct README. -1 the text input has no label (placeholder only); -1 checkbox and delete labels don't name the task. -4 speed: 18 minutes against the 5-minute target. -1 DX: needs Node 22+ and a hand-written settings file to use a Gemini key headlessly.
- [Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code): Anthropic's agentic coding tool that works in your terminal, IDE and codebase. Free tier: No. Pricing: Paid Claude plan or Anthropic API usage. Test score: Untested: paid plan only
- [OpenAI Codex](https://openai.com/codex/): OpenAI's coding agent across ChatGPT, the cloud, the IDE extension and the terminal. Free tier: No. Pricing: Included with paid ChatGPT plans (from $20/mo Plus). Test score: Untested: paid plan only
- [Replit](https://replit.com): Cloud development platform whose Replit Agent builds and deploys apps from a prompt. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free starter usage + paid plans (Core from $20/mo). Test score: Untested: login blocked from our test machine
- [Windsurf](https://windsurf.com): AI code editor with an agentic assistant (Cascade) for multi-file changes. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free plan + paid plans. Test score: Untested: free credits exhausted
- [Zed](https://zed.dev): Fast open-source code editor with built-in AI agent editing. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free editor + paid AI plans. Test score: Untested: agent runs only in the desktop app

## New this week (found by our discovery agents 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-29; listed, not yet tested or scored)
- [Floorplan](https://github.com/haydenschmitty/floorplan): Claude Code / Codex plugin that reads your codebase and draws an interactive, plain-English map of every part, file and web request, then shows which parts the agent touched after each change. MIT, zero dependencies, runs locally with no telemetry; questions go through your own Claude or Codex account. Live demo at haydenschmitty.github.io/floorplan-demo. Created Oct 27, 2026 (v0.2.2 Oct 29). Found 2026-10-29.
- [MCode Stack (MiniMax)](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/mcode-stack): The MiniMax Code team's own open-sourced workflows: 17 SKILL.md skills and checklists (independent review, subagent-split check, long-session check, small PRs, tool-budget audit and more). MIT; installs as a plugin marketplace in Claude Code or Codex, or copies into ~/.agents/skills. Released Oct 28, 2026. Found 2026-10-29.
- [DevBox (RudderStack)](https://github.com/rudderlabs/devbox): Self-hosted autonomous engineering harness: hand it a ticket (CLI or Linear) and it plans, codes, runs tests, reviews its own diff and opens a draft PR, one sandbox per task with placeholder tokens swapped in by an egress proxy. MIT; runs on Docker Compose or Kubernetes with your own OpenAI or Anthropic key (model usage is billed by your provider). Open-sourced Oct 27, 2026. Found 2026-10-29.
- [Our Silly Games](https://oursilly.games): Make a browser game by chatting with Claude Code or Codex, then publish it with free hosting, realtime multiplayer and leaderboards. MIT plugin (kirkness/osg-plugin) with 11 game-making skills; publishing needs a free Our Silly Games sign-in. Product Hunt Oct 27, 2026. Found 2026-10-28.
- [trompe + anymove (patch.gg)](https://github.com/patch-gg/trompe): Two Apache-2.0 game-art pipelines from patch.gg: trompe textures a whole gray-box game level with image models (glTF out), and anymove (github.com/patch-gg/anymove) turns one AI video into a GLB animation for any rigged creature. Code is free; the image/video models run on paid APIs (their demo level cost about $4.44 on fal). Released Oct 25 and 27, 2026. Found 2026-10-28.
- [Nyxis](https://github.com/NyxFoundation/nyxis): Lean backend framework for apps written by AI agents: you write and approve Cedar authorization policies, the agent writes handlers, and every build checks a formal proof that no request sequence can leak or modify data beyond permissions. MIT, v0.1, under active development. Created Oct 26, 2026. Found 2026-10-28.
- [Hob](https://hob.chat/): Free, open-source (MIT) desktop app that runs open-weight models like Gemma and gpt-oss on your own computer, as an offline, private alternative to Claude and ChatGPT; no account or subscription. FrigadeHQ/hob; Show HN Oct 26 (144 pts), v0.2 released Oct 26. Mac, Windows, Linux. Found 2026-10-27.
- [desigma](https://github.com/deepfounder-ai/desigma): Free, open-source (MIT/Apache-2.0), offline Figma alternative written in Rust, with a local MCP server so coding agents can inspect designs, edit them and generate code; imports Figma files. Early alpha (first release Oct 11); Product Hunt #9 on Oct 26. Found 2026-10-27.
- [GEOInflow](https://github.com/yaojingang/GEOInflow): Self-hosted analytics (MIT) that shows which AI crawlers and AI search engines visit your site, which pages they request or miss, and what traffic AI search sends you. Open-sourced Oct 26, 2026. Found 2026-10-27.
- [Corgi](https://corgi.computer/): Terminal multiplexer for humans and coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode): shows which agent is working or needs you, keeps sessions running like tmux, tracks tokens and file changes. MIT (tals/corgi); Show HN Oct 23 (138 pts). macOS, Linux, WSL. Found 2026-10-26.
- [Farol](https://winnin.github.io/farol/): Free, open-source CLI and GitHub Action that maps the risk of a pull request after AI review: riskiest files, what they reach, diff coverage and contract breaks (TS/React, Go, Python). MIT (winnin/farol); Show HN Oct 25. Found 2026-10-26.
- [AgentValley](https://agentvalley.app): Free macOS notch app that shows every Claude Code session and sub-agent at a glance (model, working or waiting on you), each with a pixel programmer. MIT (morsechimwai/agent-valley); Product Hunt #4 on Oct 24. Found 2026-10-26.
- [tstack (Theo / t3dotgg)](https://github.com/t3dotgg/tstack): Theo's everyday agent skills for Claude Code and Codex: full-send PR flow, multi-model 'council' review, babysit-PR through CI, take over someone else's PR. MIT; published Oct 24. Needs an authenticated gh CLI. Found 2026-10-26.
- [BeautifulRust](https://github.com/morganlinton/BeautifulRust): Claude Code plugin that teaches Claude to write idiomatic, robust Rust. MIT; created Oct 23, 900+ stars in its first days. Found 2026-10-26.
- [xss-audit skill](https://github.com/songjianyang/xss-audit): Agent skill that runs a 14-layer static XSS audit on React, TypeScript and JavaScript projects. MIT; created Oct 24. A useful second check on AI-written front-end code. Found 2026-10-26.
- [Halv](https://halv.ai): Desktop workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex, Kimi and GLM side by side on the plans you already pay for, with a local proxy that trims context tokens and a live savings meter. The app and its local engine went open source (Apache-2.0) on Oct 22; only the optional Halv Cloud router is paid. macOS first; Show HN Oct 22. Found 2026-10-23.
- [Recursive Flint + rec](https://github.com/recursive-oss/rec): Flint is a local coding model from Recursive with open weights on Hugging Face (Apache-2.0); rec is its Apache-2.0 inference engine with ready-made launchers for Pi and OpenCode. Needs an Apple Silicon M4 Pro/M5 Pro/M5 Max with 48 GB+ memory. Released Oct 21. Found 2026-10-23.
- [Rossark Motion skill](https://github.com/rossark0/rossark-motion-skill): Claude Code skill that turns any SVG drawing into a smooth 60 fps animation (breathing, blinking, full-body acting, whole scenes) in React Native and SwiftUI. Handy for app and game illustrations. MIT; created Oct 22, trending on GitHub. Found 2026-10-23.
- [3D Model Anything (Wes Bos)](https://github.com/wesbos/3d-model-anything): iPhone LiDAR + photo capture app, a Three.js viewer and a scan-to-threejs agent skill that guides a coding agent through rebuilding a real room as an editable 3D scene. Good fit for game devs and Three.js tinkerers. Code MIT (demo assets under a separate license); created Oct 21. Found 2026-10-23.

## Retests and attempts with no score (scores only change after a complete, fair run)
- 2026-10-29, Goose and Qwen Code: Postponed again; scores unchanged (94 and 93). Four 1-token test requests to gemini-3.8-flash on the free tier between 04:02 and 04:11 CDT: one answered after 84 seconds and three timed out after 90 seconds, so we didn't start either run (fourth morning in a row). A full agent run makes dozens of model calls, so it wouldn't be a fair test at that speed.
- 2026-10-28, Goose and Qwen Code: Postponed again; scores unchanged (94 and 93). Four 1-token test requests to gemini-3.8-flash on the free tier between 04:02 and 04:08 CDT: two returned 503 'high demand' errors and two timed out after 90 seconds, so we didn't start either run (third morning in a row). We retested OpenCode instead, which needs no model key.
- 2026-10-27, Goose and Qwen Code: Postponed; scores unchanged (94 and 93). Planned retests on a quieter Gemini day. Three 1-token test requests to gemini-3.8-flash on the free tier between 04:02 and 04:11 CDT got no answer (timed out after 120, 90 and 60 seconds), so we didn't start either run.
- 2026-10-26, Goose: No result; score unchanged (94). Retest of Goose CLI 1.56.0 on gemini-3.8-flash. The first model reply took 504 s, then the Gemini free tier returned three 503 errors and Goose exited with a network error before writing any files. Not a fair test, so no new score.
